name: snes9x (synchronous, no ASYNCIFY)
role: Real-time routing/playback. DEFAULT boot core. Paired with the bsnes-mercury cores which stay available for paused, frame-perfect sub-pixel work.
license: Non-commercial (Snes9x license); see the snes9x source LICENSE.

asyncify.why: snes9x does NOT use libco cooperative cothreads the way bsnes does, so retro_run is a normal SYNCHRONOUS call that returns each frame with NO ASYNCIFY. That is the whole performance point: real-time playback on the mobile main thread. Verified by tools/run-smoke.mjs — retro_run returns each frame synchronously and the JS loader contains zero 'asyncify' references.

optimization: Built with AGGRESSIVE optimization: -O3 -flto -DNDEBUG on BOTH compile (CFLAGS/CXXFLAGS) AND link (LDFLAGS). The prior build shipped with NO explicit optimization level at LINK and -flto CLEARED (the emscripten block set `LTO :=`), so Emscripten's link/codegen step ran effectively unoptimized — the dominant cause of the ~26 FPS cap on device. Rebuilding with -O3 -flto at both stages produced a SMALLER, faster core: .wasm dropped from 3347860 to 2910410 bytes (~13%). -flto linked cleanly (no thin-LTO fallback needed).
verified: tools/run-smoke.mjs cores/snes9x_libretro.js 300 — ALL ASSERTIONS PASSED: retro_load_game true, retro_run returns each frame with NO hang, video_refresh non-null 256x224 RGB565, frames advance. WRAM (RETRO_MEMORY_SYSTEM_RAM) size = 131072. NO ASYNCIFY (synchronous retro_run — the performance point) preserved. Headless Node timing (forced --liftoff-only baseline compiler, which under-represents -O3's on-device win) ~0.95 ms/frame after vs ~0.99 ms/frame before; the meaningful speedup is on iOS Safari's optimizing WASM tier where -O3 -flto matters most and can only be measured on-device.
hud_memory_map: EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED IDENTICAL to bsnes. snes9x exposes the same standard 128KB SNES WRAM (RETRO_MEMORY_SYSTEM_RAM = 131072 bytes), and tools/hud-calibrate.mjs run against cores/snes9x_libretro.js passes every SMB1 (All-Stars) physics proof at the SAME offsets as bsnes ($005D H-Speed, $0042/$0043/$0401 X, $0002/$041C Y). The earlier '(unverified)/does-not-track' note came from a weakness in tools/hud-crosscheck.mjs (it could not drive Mario into free motion), NOT a real WRAM-layout difference. memory-watch.js treats all cores as sharing the one verified map (CALIBRATION_VERIFIED = true); the frame counter (engine-sourced) is always correct on every core.
emscripten_flags: NO -s ASYNCIFY (synchronous retro_run — the performance win)
-s EXPORTED_FUNCTIONS=[22 raw retro_* + malloc/free; NO retro_cheat_*]
single-threaded (no pthreads / no SharedArrayBuffer) for iOS
makefile_edits: Added an 'else ifeq ($(platform), emscripten)' block to snes9x/libretro/Makefile modeled on the bsnes-mercury emscripten block but WITHOUT ASYNCIFY: CC=emcc/CXX=em++/LD=em++, fpic cleared, -fno-strict-aliasing, TARGET=snes9x_libretro.js, and the SHARED link flags above. The block now sets OPTIMIZE := -O3 -flto -DNDEBUG and appends it to CFLAGS, CXXFLAGS AND LDFLAGS (LTO requires the flag at link too) and restores LTO := -flto; the earlier build cleared LTO and added no link-time -O, so the WASM shipped unoptimized. Built with `emmake make platform=emscripten -j8` (emsdk 6.0.9).
